topic.name: Simplifying Rational Expressions Using Polynomial Factorization

question.text: Which of the following is equivalent to $\dfrac{3n^2 + 15n + 18} {n^2 + 4n + 4}?$
question.explanation:
We factor the numerator and denominator, canceling out any common factors that appear in both.

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ \dfrac{3n^2 + 15n + 18} {n^2 + 4n + 4} &=\dfrac{3(n^2 + 5n + 6)} {n^2 + 4n + 4}\\ &=\dfrac{3(n + 3)(n + 2)} {(n + 2)(n + 2)}\\ &=\dfrac{3(n + 3)\cancel{(n + 2)}} {(n + 2)\cancel{(n + 2)}} \\ &=\dfrac {3(n + 3)} {n + 2}\\ &=\dfrac {3n + 9} {n + 2}. } \]

example.title: Simplifying a Rational Expression by Factoring Second-Order Polynomials in Both the Numerator and Denominator

question.text: What is $\dfrac{5 h^2 - 10 h - 75} {h + 3}$ reduced to lowest terms?
question.explanation:
The numerator can be factored as \[ 5 h^2 - 10 h - 75 = 5(h^2 - 2h - 15) = 5(h - 5)(h + 3). \] Canceling out any common factors that appear in the numerator and the denominator, we get

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ \dfrac{5 h^2 - 10 h - 75} {h + 3} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{5(h - 5)(h + 3)} {h + 3} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac{5(h-5)\cancel{(h + 3)}} {\cancel{h + 3}} & = \\[5pt] \dfrac {5(h - 5)}{1} & = \\[5pt] 5h - 25 &. } \]

example.title: Simplifying a Rational Expression by Factoring a Second-Order Polynomial in the Numerator

question.explanation:
The numerator can be factored as $wy + 6y = y(w + 6)$ and the denominator can be factored as $w^2 + 2 w - 24 = (w + 6)(w - 4).$ Canceling out any common factors that appear in the numerator and the denominator, we get

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ \dfrac{wy + 6y} {w^2 + 2 w - 24} & = \dfrac{y(w + 6)} {(w + 6)(w - 4)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{y\cancel{(w + 6)}} {\cancel{(w + 6)}(w - 4)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{y} {w - 4} . } \]
